EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
Tensions in the Middle East have significantly escalated with the revelation of a secret Israeli military base in Iraq, allegedly used for air operations against Iran, and Iran’s explicit threats to heavily retaliate against any aggression towards its maritime vessels in the Strait of Hormuz. These developments unfold amid an ongoing US naval blockade against Iran and persistent cross-border exchanges between Hezbollah and Israel, which saw three Israeli reservists wounded by a Hezbollah drone.

IRAN
IRGC Aerospace Force Commander Brigadier General Seyyed Majid Moosavi declared that Iran's missiles and drones are "locked on the American targets and enemy ships in the region" and are "awaiting the command to fire." The IRGC Navy warned that "any act of aggression against Iranian oil tankers or commercial vessels will result in a heavy attack against American bases in the region and enemy ships." A spokesperson for Khatam HQ stated, "Strait of Hormuz: Entry of dogs or Americans is forbidden," and Iran threatened to cut global internet cables under the Strait of Hormuz if necessary. Internally, the Ministry of Communications reported $335 million in direct damages to the ICT sector due to the ongoing 11-week nationwide internet shutdown, which has also pushed virtual businesses to street vending. Judicial authorities seized assets of 264 opponents. Russia's President Putin affirmed Iran's trustworthiness in nuclear matters, stating Iran has no goal of weaponizing uranium and citing a religious fatwa. Putin also expressed Russia's readiness to repeat the storage of enriched uranium for Iran, but noted a hardened US stance. Economically, global oil inventories are at their lowest since 2018, and the Caspian Sea has become a critical trade route for Iran to bypass the US naval blockade, with Russia supplying essential goods and drone components. Foreign Minister Ali Safari stated Iran is reviewing the US response to de-escalation proposals and claims the US has no right to use the Strait of Hormuz for attacks.

ISRAEL
Israeli forces intercepted suspicious aerial targets and several hostile drones launched from Lebanon in the Western Galilee, triggering sirens in Hanita, Shlomi, Ya'ara, Metzuba, Betzet, Rosh HaNikra, Lehman, Hof Achziv, and Baram. A rocket from Lebanon struck an open area near Baram, causing no injuries. IDF strikes targeted over 85 Hezbollah infrastructures in southern Lebanon, including weapon depots, rocket launchers, and an underground weapons manufacturing site in the Beqaa Valley. In the Gaza Strip, the IDF and Shin Bet destroyed a Palestinian Islamic Jihad (PIJ) weapon manufacturing site in northern Gaza, which Hamas also utilized.
Casualties include three IDF reservists wounded by an explosive drone launched by Hezbollah near the Lebanese border; one sustained serious injuries, while an officer and another soldier were moderately wounded. An unmanned engineering vehicle in southern Lebanon was also damaged by an explosive drone.
The Wall Street Journal reported that Israel established a clandestine military outpost in the Iraqi desert, with US knowledge, to support its air campaign against Iran. This base was reportedly used to fire upon Iraqi soldiers who nearly discovered it, resulting in one Iraqi soldier's death. PM Netanyahu reportedly warned the US against prolonged negotiations with Iran and deemed any agreement that does not fully dismantle Iran's nuclear program unacceptable.

GAZA & WEST BANK
IDF forces, in cooperation with Shin Bet, destroyed a weapon manufacturing and storage site belonging to Palestinian Islamic Jihad in the northern Gaza Strip on May 9th, which was also used by Hamas. Hezbollah offered condolences to Hamas following the assassination of a senior leader's son in an Israeli airstrike in eastern Gaza. The United Nations reported that Israeli military attacks and settler violence displaced approximately 40,000 Palestinians in the occupied West Bank over the past year. Hamas condemned alleged "torture and abuse" of Palestinian women in Israeli jails, labeling them as war crimes. A Palestinian Christian delegation warned the EU about threats to their community in Gaza due to Israeli policies.

LEBANON
Hezbollah launched multiple offensive operations, including explosive drones that wounded three IDF reservists (one seriously) and damaged an unmanned engineering vehicle near the Israeli border. Hezbollah FPV drones were also spotted in Metula and used to target Israeli soldiers and a Merkava tank in Bayada. In response, Israel's IDF conducted extensive strikes, hitting over 85 Hezbollah targets in southern Lebanon and an underground weapons manufacturing site in the Beqaa Valley. Specific Israeli airstrikes were reported in Bedyas and Al-Saksakieh, with Press TV and Naya reporting 11 civilian casualties, including a child and her mother, in Al-Saksakieh. An Israeli drone strike on a road in Meltaka Al-Nahrin, Chouf entrance, also reportedly resulted in 3 martyrs.

SYRIA & IRAQ
The Wall Street Journal reported that Israel established a secret temporary military base in the Iraqi desert, with US knowledge, to support air operations against Iran. Israeli forces reportedly fired on Iraqi soldiers who almost exposed the base, killing one. US fighter jets and AH-64 Apache helicopters were heard flying over Baghdad, with suspicious US Air Force activity reported over the Samawa desert. Iraqi border guards seized an air balloon carrying 34 kg of Captagon pills from Syria. A governmental committee in Iraq is reportedly nearing completion of a plan to disarm pro-Iranian militias, which is intended to be presented to the Trump administration.

GULF STATES
Bahrain announced the arrest of 41 individuals linked to Iran's IRGC for allegedly sympathizing with Iran. Saudi Arabia's Foreign Ministry expressed full support for Bahrain's actions. This was met by an Iranian MP's warning to Bahrain not to "risk closing the Strait of Hormuz forever" by supporting a US-led UN resolution against Iran. Qatar's Foreign Minister met with US Secretary of State Rubio and Saudi Foreign Minister Mohammed bin Abd al-Rahman to discuss de-escalation between Iran and the US and regional stability. Gulf states reportedly spent $17 billion on 4,200 Patriot missiles, indicating preparations for potential conflict. An analyst suggested the UAE left OPEC to increase oil output and recover economic losses, potentially pushing global prices down. A Qatari LNG carrier was observed navigating an Iran-approved route through the Strait of Hormuz, marking the first such passage since the war began in February. US CENTCOM claimed its naval blockade against Iran remains fully in effect, having diverted 58 vessels and disabled 4.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **Secret Israeli Base in Iraq:** The Wall Street Journal reported Israel established a clandestine military outpost in the Iraqi desert, with US knowledge, to support air operations against Iran, leading to one Iraqi soldier's death when Israeli forces fired upon Iraqis who neared the base.
2.  **Hezbollah Drone Attack on Israel:** Three IDF reservists were wounded, one seriously, by an explosive drone launched by Hezbollah at northern Israel near the Lebanese border on May 9th.
3.  **Iran's Strait of Hormuz Threats:** IRGC Aerospace Force Commander Moosavi stated Iranian missiles and drones are "locked on American targets" and the IRGC Navy threatened "heavy attack" against US assets for any aggression against Iranian vessels. Iran also threatened to cut global internet cables in the Strait.
4.  **US Naval Blockade vs. Iranian Evasion:** US CENTCOM asserted its full naval blockade of Iran, having diverted 58 vessels and disabled 4. Iran is reportedly using the Caspian Sea and ship-to-ship transfers to circumvent these measures.
5.  **Bahrain Arrests and Regional Pressure:** Bahrain arrested 41 individuals linked to Iran's IRGC, with Saudi Arabia's support. An Iranian MP retaliated with a threat to Bahrain over its stance on a US-led UN resolution concerning the Strait of Hormuz.
6.  **Diplomacy and Deadlines:** US Secretary of State Rubio indicated an expectation for Iran's response to an agreement proposal by May 9th. Trump claimed Iran is eager for a deal but warned of "Operation Freedom Plus" if negotiations fail, while Netanyahu urged against prolonged talks.
7.  **Extensive IDF Strikes:** Israel conducted over 85 strikes against Hezbollah targets in southern Lebanon and the Beqaa Valley, and destroyed a PIJ weapon manufacturing site in northern Gaza Strip on May 9th.
8.  **Regional Military Posturing:** The UK is redeploying HMS Dragon to the Middle East to potentially join a multinational effort to secure the Strait of Hormuz, complementing a French carrier strike group already in the region.
9.  **Global Economic Impact:** The conflict has led to global oil inventories falling to their lowest since 2018, and economists warn of rising costs to households in developed economies.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
Escalation risks remain high, particularly in the Strait of Hormuz, given Iran's explicit threats of "heavy attack" for any aggression against its vessels and the US maintaining its blockade. The revelation of a secret Israeli base in Iraq, and the engagement with Iraqi forces, significantly raises the risk of regional spillover and potential direct confrontation with Iraq or Iranian-backed militias, directly involving the US. Cross-border exchanges between Hezbollah and Israel are active flashpoints, as demonstrated by the recent injury of IDF reservists. Red lines are clearly drawn: Iran views any aggression against its maritime vessels as grounds for severe retaliation, while the US and Israel prioritize preventing Iran from obtaining nuclear weapons.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
The **US** posture is characterized by a continued naval blockade against Iran and diplomatic efforts via Secretary of State Rubio with Qatar and Saudi Arabia for de-escalation. President Trump expressed that Iran "very much" desires a deal but warned of a "Freedom Plus" operation if talks fail. **Gulf States** are reacting to threats, with Bahrain arresting 41 individuals linked to the IRGC, supported by Saudi Arabia, and spending $17 billion on Patriot missiles. Qatar is actively engaged in mediation efforts. The **UK** is redeploying HMS Dragon to the Middle East for potential Strait of Hormuz security, aligning with **France**, which already has a carrier strike group deployed. **Russia**'s President Putin believes the Ukraine war is ending and is close to a major gas/oil deal with China. Russia has also been aiding Iran by shipping drone components and other goods via the Caspian Sea, while Putin hopes the Iran-US conflict ends quickly and maintains dialogue with both sides.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
Contradictions persist in reporting, particularly regarding the status of the Strait of Hormuz, with Press TV claiming no commercial traffic in 24 hours while other sources report a Qatari LNG carrier's passage and CENTCOM asserts an active blockade. Conflicting reports also emerged from Ukraine regarding ceasefire adherence. The existence of a secret Israeli base in Iraq, while widely reported, lacks official confirmation from the involved parties. Unverified claims include explosions in Sirjan, Tehran, and Bandar Abbas, and an improbable claim by an IRGC official about Mossad using "genies." Propaganda indicators are present in both Iranian and US messaging, with Iran emphasizing its military strength and national unity, and Trump employing AI-generated images and strong rhetoric. Reporting gaps include specific details of US-Iran negotiations and unconfirmed civilian casualty figures from Israeli strikes in Lebanon.
